subject: Re: PO field requirements and discount options for CoreHealth
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@corehealth.co>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@corehealth.co
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: CoreHealth PO template + net terms request

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the update on pricing last week. Procurement asked me to send over our PO template and a couple of constraints we need cleared before we can move to contracting:

- Net terms: CoreHealth standard is net90 for third-party vendors with no prepayment.
- Invoice cadence: we require consolidated monthly invoices by billing_entity_id (one invoice per month per billing_entity_id).
- PO metadata: every invoice line must include PO number, project_code, and cost_center fields so our AP system can ingest automatically.
- Financial approvals: we need an explicit vendor VAT/Tax ID on invoices and a PO acknowledgement from your side.

I've attached our PO template (CoreHealth_PO_Template_v2.pdf). Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the field mapping above, and whether any of these requirements would affect discount eligibility or require a different pricing structure.

Best,
Elena Morales
Sr. Procurement Manager
CoreHealth

Attachment: CoreHealth_PO_Template_v2.pdf (PDF, 214 KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@corehealth.co>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CoreHealth PO template + net terms request

Hi Elena — thanks for the template and the clear list. We can support the majority of the fields you mention, but a few items will affect how we structure the discount:

- PO metadata: we can populate PO number, project_code, cost_center and billing_entity_id on all invoice lines. We will need the exact field names used in your ERP (you used project_code vs project-id in the PDF). I attached our PO field mapping for your AP team to review.
- Net terms: current standard for this commercial offer is net45. Moving to net90 materially increases credit exposure for us; to accommodate a longer term we typically require either a committed spend or a prepayment/escrow.
- Invoice cadence: we can do consolidated monthly invoices per billing_entity_id. Weekly or daily invoicing increases processing overhead and could change the unit price.

If CoreHealth cannot prepay or commit up front, we can propose a mid-ground: net60 with a limited discount (3%) if PO includes the required metadata and a 12-month minimum commitment. If CoreHealth can agree to quarterly prepayment we can extend an 8% discount.

I'm attaching Redwood_PO_Field_Mapping.xlsx with suggested column names. Can your AP team review and confirm the exact header names? If helpful, we can do a 20-min call later this week to walk the mapping and finalize the tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_PO_Field_Mapping.xlsx (Excel, 42 KB)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@corehealth.co>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CoreHealth PO template + net terms request

Elena — looping in a quick pricing note from our side so requirements are explicit.

Short version: we want to keep CoreHealth as a strategic customer and are prepared to be flexible on terms if there's an operational trade (commitment or prepay) that offsets credit exposure. Proposed options:

- Option A (preferred for CoreHealth economics): Quarterly prepayment -> 8% list discount + no change to unit pricing.
- Option B (middle ground): Net60, monthly consolidated invoices, full PO metadata present -> 3% discount, requires 12-month minimum committed spend (you can ramp).
- Option C: Net90 (no prepay/commit) -> no enterprise discount; standard per-unit rates apply and payment review cadence every 90 days.

Operational constraints we need enforced in the PO to accept any discount:
- billing_entity_id must match our invoice header and be present on the PO.
- GL/ERP mapping: PO must expose a project_code and cost_center per line (exact header names to be confirmed).
- VAT/tax identifier must be on the vendor profile and printed on each invoice.

If CoreHealth wants to stay with net90 but expects a deep discount, we will need an offset such as a multi-year commitment or an early payment guarantee.

Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow; Mateo, can you propose 30 minutes?

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@corehealth.co>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@corehealth.co
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CoreHealth PO template + net terms request

Thanks Mateo and Tessa. I appreciate the options — a few quick notes from Procurement: 

- Prepayment is not possible under our policy for new vendors. We can consider conditional prepay after a vendor has been live for a full quarter and proven delivery.
- We could stretch to net75, but net60 is the outside limit for our AP cycle only with CFO approval. Net90 is our default for non-prepay vendors but we'd prefer to keep the term as short as possible.
- We will not do a mandatory 12-month pre-commit as a blanket — any minimums must be tied to measurable spend forecasts and must be in the SOW.

Operationally, we can accept the PO metadata requirement (project_code and cost_center per line), but the field names are fixed in our ERP. Please review the attached Procurement_Policy_CoreHealth_2026.pdf and align headers in your mapping exactly (we can't accept alias headers).

Can Redwood confirm whether a net75 cadence with monthly consolidated invoices (one invoice per billing_entity_id) would trigger the 3% discount, assuming PO field names are exact and we can agree an initial 3-month forecast in the SOW?

Best,
Elena

Attachment: Procurement_Policy_CoreHealth_2026.pdf (PDF, 128 KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@corehealth.co>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CoreHealth PO template + net terms request — Redwood position

Hi Elena — thanks for the clarity and for sending your procurement policy. Quick summary from Redwood so we can close the loop:

1) We will accept CoreHealth's PO metadata requirements exactly as written in your procurement policy; our finance team will mirror the ERP header names.

2) Discount trigger: Redwood will commit to a 3% commercial discount if the following are true:
   - Net75 payment terms,
   - Monthly consolidated invoices per billing_entity_id,
   - PO includes exact header names for project_code and cost_center per your ERP,
   - A 3-month initial forecasted spend is included in the SOW (non-binding forecast that maps to billing ramps).

3) If CoreHealth can move to quarterly prepayment we will maintain the 8% discount option (we understand that is currently not possible).

4) We'll send a short SOW addendum that captures the 3-month forecast and the invoice header mapping so Procurement and Legal can sign off. Attached is a short summary doc (SOW_minimum_commitment_summary.pdf) that we can use as the basis for the addendum.

If that captures your position, can we lock the agreement and route a PO acknowledgement? If you'd rather discuss, we can set a 30-minute call next week.

Thanks and looking forward to closing this — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_minimum_commitment_summary.pdf (PDF, 55 KB)
